utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dan Saxon, Barney Thomas, and Ms. Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. I'm Novak Lukic, and Gregor Guy-Smith, Tina Drolec, and Boris Zorko are part of the team representing General Perisic with me here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Lukic. Good afternoon, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope you had a restful weekend and ready to move this afternoon. Just to remind you, that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, good afternoon, once again, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are still within the realm of what is now Prosecution 65 ter XN-132, which is -- falls within the term of art "fresh evidence," and that's where we will probably continue for a large part of this particular session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I believe we remain within the same discussion as regards fresh evidence, which is being offered for purposes of impeachment only, which is the reason why I'm asking the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It doesn't have to be stated every time we talk about it Mr. Guy-Smith. Once it has been stated that it is tendered for purposes of impeachment only --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- that's enough. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yeah, I think there are certain things that don't always have to be mentioned at certain times, but be that as it may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I am -- we need the second Drina binder to be provided to Mr. Simic. And for now, I am going to skip tab 9. And, Mr. Simic, if you could turn to tab 10 in your binder, please. It's page 33 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we should now be in seeing in XN-1 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We should now be seeing XN-132, e-court - hopefully - page 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General Simic, if we can just focus on the first page, please. We see "People's Defence, state secret" at the top, the word "Drina," and then this says "copy number 1," does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this is an excerpt from the directive on the use of the army of Republika Srpska, is that right, is that what the title says in the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's dated December 1993. The bottom of the page we see the stamp of the VRS Main Staff. It says "copy number 1" at the top. Is that because the -- this was found -- this particular document was -- was found in the possession of -- or came from the binder of the Drina Corps. So would the original stay with the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is quite unclear to me. It's unclear to add to it. I'm being pointed -- connected with the Drina Corps, and I'm seeing the cover page which states excerpt from the directives for the use of the army of Republika Srpska. So I'm not sure what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My mistake, General, if my question was wasn't clear. This came from a binder or folder marked "Drina Corps." This is what we looked at this last week. My question for you, sir, is: Copy number 1, can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that documents are done in two copies. One copy is kept for distribution, and the other one should go to the command which should carry out the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And if you turn to the last page, General --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honours, I'm not sure that the interpretation, the witness said for the -- for the person who is working it out. It's not distribution. Perhaps the interpreters could explain. Perhaps the witness could explain what he means exactly by this term "razradjivac" because this term is quite specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you help us, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps the second part of your last response requires a bit more explanation, Mr. Simic. You said that one copy is kept for distribution. And the other one should go to the command which should carry out the task. So does this extra extract that we see in front of us, is this a copy sent to a particular command so that the task is carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, this document was developed in the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, and one copy remains at the Main Staff, and the second copy is sent to the subordinates for the implementation of the assignment. Last time, I used the term razradjivac meaning the person who developed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does that satisfy Your Honour and Mr. Lukic? I see him nodding his head. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have nothing to be satisfied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm glad then, Your Honour. And if we can please go to page 49 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see when the document should be implemented by, the 28th of December, 1993, and signed by Commander Ratko Mladic, and the stamp of the VRS Main Staff. Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can then turn to page 50 in e-court. And if you could turn to the next tab in your binder, which, I believe, is a black and white copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on e-court, will see, Your Honours, it's not so easy to read. I have brought colour hard copies, one of which I have given already to the Defence. If could I ask the usher's assistance, please, to give a copy to Mr. Lukic. And I've got three copies for the Bench as well, to make it easier for the Bench to follow along. Mr. Lukic already has his? Yes. I'm sorry, one for the witness and three for the Judges. I have an additional copy if the Chamber or the Chamber's legal officer would like one, Your Honour, I'm in your hands. I see the legal officer nodding, so there we are. And if we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is just one copy. But if there is one, a spare one, perhaps it would be good to provide one for General Perisic who was not able to see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, now I don't have any additional copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right, never mind. We will look at it together at the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Next time I will bring at least one more copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, you will see this is a map. What does it say in the middle at the top, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it states: Excerpt from the decision on the use of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see this map has been signed and approved by Ratko Mladic in the upper left-hand corner. And in the bottom right-hand corner, we see that it's been signed by General Milovanovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. To be precise, I just would like that add in the upper left-hand corner it states, Approved by the commander, Ratko Mladic. And in the right hand bottom corner, Processed by the Chief of Staff, Manojlo Milovanovic. This is essential in all our correspondence and working through of a document. I'm thinking about the procedure for documents in the Army of Yugoslavia. And they adopted the same method of work, according to the directions from the former JNA. We continued to apply the same instructions until we developed new -- a new set of instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that, General Simic. And remaining with the signature of General Milovanovic in the bottom right-hand corner, you mention that this shows it has been processed by General Milovanovic. By "processed," would it be fair to say that General Milovanovic signed off on the final version of this map that was forwarded to General Mladic for his approval?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The final draft, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And approximately how many men --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately how many officers get involved in the drafting, in the production of a map like this, for a directive like Drina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, just to avoid the objection that the witness was speculating, I would like more precision when a question of this type is being put. Either is how many people would be -- a project like this where he worked, or in principle how many people would be employed on a project like this. This is just out of caution so that the witness would not be put the position to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I don't want to you speculate. But in your knowledge and experience, and on Friday, you talked about particular documents that required the input of a number of officers. And I'm just wondering, whether, for example, pursuant to your knowledge and experience, does a map like this take the input of one or two officers or more?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, all that I'm telling you, you're asking me about the documents of the army of Republika Srpska and I'm answering on the basis of my experience in the Army of Yugoslavia. But, in view of the fact that we completed the same schools, I assume that the same practice was continued. And let me answer the question specifically. When this type of key documents are drafted, such as a decision by the Main Staff, the whole staff and all the assistants and -- of the commander of the Main Staff and other assistants are involved in the drafting of such a document. But I would be able to state that with full responsibility when we're talking about documents such as this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And can you tell us, please, in summary form, what does -- what does this map depict? What are we seeing here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map depicts the concept or decision of the Main Staff about the use of the army of Republika Srpska over a longer period of the war. If you look in the lower left-hand corner, it states "key," and then below that it says first stage of the operation and second phase of the operation. The operations are carried out over a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see on this map -- first of all, we see some different colours. We see some areas that are shaded in sort of a light -- a yellowish light green colour; we see broken red lines; up towards the top of the document, we appear to see some broken black lines. Can you explain what these different colours and lines indicate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I've read the key with a specific purpose. In the first phase, there is one sub-colour, which corresponds to the sub-colour on the map. Then we have the second phase, with another sub-colour, which corresponds to the activities of the army of Republika Srpska in this second face. That is exactly what this marks. These broken lines that you asked about with an arrow mean that the forces of the army of Republika Srpska should attain those positions at that particular stage or phase of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And because many of us in this room are unable to read this document in your language, when you refer to the key in the bottom left-hand side, indicating the two phases and the colour, which colour refers to the first phase, and which colour refers to the second phase, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The yellow colour represents the first phase, and this reddish-orange colour would stand for the second phase. But let us be clear here: All the units do not have to take part in each of the phases. Some of the units can participate in both phases while some units can only participate in one of the phases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Speaking of different units depicted on this map, in the middle of the map, a little bit below the halfway point, we see the word "Sarajevo." Which units are depicted around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We have another map for General Perisic. I'm grateful for Ms. Javier for organised that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, it's hard for me to read this. This is too small for me to be able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we see what appears to be a flag on this map, and there appear to be a number of flags, what -- what does the flag or a banner indicate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each flag has the unit number in it, and it stands for the command post of that particular unit. And as for the previous thing that you asked me about, I've read here the first Herzegovina Infantry Brigade. I made a special effort to be able to read that. If you notice the rectangle is there, and it contains the -- information about the command post of each of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, are you able to see -- well, I think that is too small for everyone. Are you able to see the enclave of Gorazde on this map, on the right-hand side, going towards the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So if the greenish-yellow colour indicates the positions of units during the first phase, and then here we see some red lines with arrows towards the town of Gorazde, does that indicate that essentially -- the army of Republika Srpska forces will have the objective of -- of moving closer around Gorazde? Is that how we would read that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the map, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. In the -- in the centre -- we see a stamp. General Simic, could you turn your focus to the upper right-hand corner, please. And can you tell us what is written in the top right-hand corner in large letters in the Cyrillic alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, sir, the upper right-hand corner reads: "All People's Defence, state secret, quotation marks, Drina, R attachment, number 1, copy number 1."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. I'd like to leave this map now. And if we could please turn to the next page in e-court, which is 51. And if you could turn to the next page in your binder, General Simic. General Simic, you'll see at the top it says: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment 6, copy number 1?" And then in the middle, I believe it says: "Extract from the plan of communications of the VRS Main Staff for the Drina Corps command." I'm sorry, it's tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little different here. At least the order is, but I think I manage to the find my way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And tab 12, the title of this document is: Extract from the plan of communication of the VRS Main Staff for Drina Corps command, does it not? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see at the bottom of that page, December 1993. And then the seal of the Drina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please -- excuse me, we saw the seal of the VRS Main Staff. I don't want to misspeak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you take a look at this page, General Simic, this is a list of documents for communication from the VRS Main Staff to the Drina Corps Command. Isn't that -- is that correct? Am I reading it correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A list of documents of the communications plan delivered to the Drina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see in the upper right-hand corner: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment 6, copy number 1." And if you could move your eyes down this list to item number 9. Item number 9 says: "Secret call-signs for Command Staffs, units, and institutions." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Code-names is what we used to call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And we're going to look at that in a moment. We see the seal of the VRS Main Staff at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, we see Drina at the top, "copy number 1." And this is an order for communications, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could -- if we could move forward two more pages, please, and scroll down to the bottom of this page, please, there we see that this order was signed by General Milovanovic. Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the other signature on -- on the page, on the bottom, on the left-hand side, Radomir Prole. In what capacity was he signing this document, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Prosecutor, it reads chief of communications, Colonel Radomir Prole. He was chief of communications in the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska. That's what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So Colonel Prole would have the task of working on such a plan of communication; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I -- I never disputed that. The chiefs of branches would normally be busy working on such documents, each within their own speciality field.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next page is a chart of radio communications from the Main Staff of the VRS. And if we scroll down, we see the stamp on the bottom. Can we go to the next page, please. On the next page, we see the overview of the time of changing frequencies. Is that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me a question that is too technical for me to explain. I'm unable to confirm this with certainty. I see that there are devices here with varying degrees of certainty, depending on the command they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General I'm very, very sorry, could you move one page forward, please. I'd like to focus on this page for the time being. And please correct me if I'm wrong, in the centre, this -- we see a chart. And this chart or table represents the -- the times for which radio frequencies should be changed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that is right. But if you're trying to tie this up with your previous question, the interpretation I got was the power of these devices, and that is what I find myself unable to confirm. Nevertheless it is quite true that the times were noted here when frequencies were switched or changed, in order to make it impossible for the enemy to monitor our radio communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Here, again, we see a -- a chart depicting the analogue radio relay communications. We see in the upper right-hand corner: "People's Defence, state secret, R, Drina, attachment number 2, copy number 1." And again we've seen a similar document previously so this particular document shows the connections between different units and -- or -- and the different radio relay stations that they use. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But there is one thing I need to set straight. We were looking at that previous chart or diagram which represented the radio communications, and this is now the radio relay communications of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this is a chart of encrypted communications, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the middle, at the -- at the top, we see a seal. And then below that we see a circle with a banner, a flag, which stands for the Drina Corps; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the upper left-hand side, we see the words "Belgrade" with a flag attached to it. And then on the upper right-hand side, we see a circle with the word "Pale" with a flag, "SRK." That would be the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us in -- actually, let me take a moment, please. We also see on the left-hand side, left from the centre, a rectangle with the word Han Pijesak. Are you able to tell us in general terms what kind of information is depicted on this chart?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This chart shows the radio relay communications for which encrypted channels were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So this chart actually indicates the encrypted channels themselves? Is that what we see here?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a technical perspective, you can see the protected or encrypted channels used for the kind of communication that needed shielding from any enemy de-scrambling equipment. So that's what I mean when I say an encrypted channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see on this page, on the upper left-hand side, some words, and I believe this says - please, correct me, General, if I'm wrong, but I believe it says, Cryptological information from the Main Staff of the VRS for the Drina Corps. Am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And we see, again, the word "Drina" on the right side, a stamp of the Main Staff in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this document is entitled: A -- an extract of an overview of special documents for encrypted communications for the Drina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Again, we see the VRS Main Staff stamp. Could you turn to the next page, please. General Simic, on this page, bears ERN 04336632, it says: "Overview of secret call-signs." Is that right? This is page 62 in the e-court. Says: "Overview of secret call-signs." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you see in item 1, the first item is the General Staff of the VJ command post; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see its call-sign "Alan," to the right. Item 2 we see General Staff of the VJ, rear command post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see its call-sign to the right, "Golija." What do the two columns on the right-hand side depict?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Column number 4, depicts the situation in which communications equipment is used to establish communication. By virtue of a line of communication being established, it doesn't mean that this same person is normally at one end of this conversation. Rather, this is a code-name that this person uses or a password, so they need to say 7590, and then the other side knows that they've just got through to the right person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Item number 3, that refers to the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Saxon. Do we now know what the other column talks about? You asked about the two last columns, now he's put an answer to one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for your intervention, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How about column number 5?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said. This is my ID caller number, which I used to identify myself to whoever happens to be at the other end of the communication line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let me ask another question, General. You described column number 4 as depicting the situation in which communications equipment is used to establish communication. Can you explain that a little bit, please. I think those of us who are following in English are having a hard time understanding.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't get more technical than this, since I'm no expert on communications equipment. What I'm telling you is my general knowledge, and I'm afraid that's as far as can I go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you find unclear and which follows from the witness's answer, perhaps because the permutation, it might be good for the witness to read number 4 and number 5, and then the interpreters can do their job, by which time I think you will have understood what the columns mean exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If could you read the title of column 4, General Simic, out loud, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, column number 4 reads abbreviated KFHX, and then number 5, 7590.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, it's my fault because my question was not clear. Could you read the title of number 4, which is just above the number 4, and the title of number 5, which is just above the number 5 at the top there.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Column 5, right above it, telegraph communications, call-sign, telegraph switchboard -- telegraph station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's actually at the top of column 4; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Column 5, it reads: "ID information." And then in the brackets, "(plate number)."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Item 3 on this list refers to the 1st Army of the VJ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Item 4, the 2nd Army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Item 5, the 3rd Army of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Item 6, the air force and anti-aircraft defence of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Item 7, the navy?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could focus your attention to item number 18 - if we could scroll down, please, on e-court - item 18, for example, refers to the Pristina Corps of the Army of Yugoslavia; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see that this document went down to the corps level of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn the page, please. Go to the next page in e-court, please. And can we focus on the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at the top of this page, General Simic, item 22, that refers to the Main Staff of the Army of Serbian Krajina, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And below that, item 23, reflects the call-signs of the Government of the Republic of Serbian Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to move on from this document now -- from this -- those pages now. And, General, if you could turn to tab 13, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could see on e-court, page 71 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this is a VRS Main Staff plan for security measures, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a plan for security measures of the VRS for both defence and attack, to be perfectly specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it has been approved by General Mladic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to tab 14, General, and go forward two more pages in e-court, page 73 in e-court. This document is entitled; anti-electronic combat, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see the word "Drina" at the top, attachment 8, copy number 7. What is the purpose of this document? Can you tell us.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of each document is to protect ourselves from any electronic operations by the enemy. The header itself reads: "Anti-electronic combat." That means keeping the enemy out of our electronic communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn to the next tab, General. And this would be page 76 in e-court. General, at the top of this page, it says: "Plan of electronic warfare." How does this document relate to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two compatible documents. One is saying that I should protect myself from any electronic action by the enemy; and the other is saying exactly the on opposite, that I should take some electronic action against their devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document that's in front of us now entitled: "Plan for electronic warfare." Does that mean that this document would describe how the army of Republika Srpska is going to jam the electronic communications of the enemy, putting it in layman's terms?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you most certainly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could move to the next tab, General, number 16, which is page 80 in e-court. This document, General, you'll see it says, "Engineering support order" at the top, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order for engineering support of the army of Republika Srpska. This is what it says, word for word.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand corner we see Drina, attachment number 10, copy number 7. If we turn to the next page, General, you will see the signature of Ratko Mladic, the signature of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The signature of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. We see the seal of the Main Staff; I spoke too quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you turn to the next page, the last page in this document - can we go one more page in e-court, please - General, are you able to help us with the notations on this -- on this page? What is being described here.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not able to help you, because I don't know what this is about. I really cannot really see it or read it, about 50 per cent of it is illegible. The arrest, if I were to read it, it would be just numbers. But I cannot really tell what exactly they refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's fine, General. Can you turn to the next tab, please. Can we go one page forward. General, this is the plan for moral and psychological activities. You will see it has been approved by General Mladic, and if you turn to the last page, you'll see -- again, this is -- and this is page 85 in e-court, the last page. You will see this is the plan that General Gvero signed which we looked at last week. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Tab 18 in your binder, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go forward in e-court, please. One more page, please. One more page. One more page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this is a plan for the use of the air force and air support of the army of Republika Srpska, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the word "plan" is not there. It's says: "The use of forces of anti-aircraft defence and air support."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for correcting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document has already been admitted as P158. So I'm not going -- well, we'll look at for a moment. Can we bring up P2158, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. When you say the next document has been admitted as P158, it is it still part of XN-132, or are you done with XN-132?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a document that is part of XN-132 that has already been admitted into evidence as 2158.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If we could look at the next document in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that's P2158.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this attachment, General, relates to logistical support, does it not, for the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would seek to tender marked for identification 65 ter XN-132, with the exception of page 32 in e-court, Your Honour. I would seek to tender the remainder of XN-132, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted XN-132, minus page 32 in e-court. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit P2894, marked for identification, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Marked for identification, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, can you turn to the next tab in your binder. It should be tab 20. And now I'd like to look at what is XN-133 in e-court. These are documents pertaining to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we ... Is this XN-133 that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: One moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apparently gave incorrect information to the Chamber on Friday. The documents related to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps begin with XN-137. And so if we can call up what is XN-137, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I understand Mr. Saxon's intent we're now moving on to a new series of documents. If such is the case, then we need an offer of proof with regard to those documents. I don't know whether these documents are being offered for the same purposes as previous documents, those being Drina Corps documents for impeachment only, or whether or not Mr. Saxon is taking a different position with regard to these documents. When we had our last discussion he was focussed on the Drina Corps documents. Now he is dealing with a different set of documents. So I think we need to have an understanding from the Prosecution as to what their position is with regard to these documents under the decisional law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, on Friday, I sought leave from the Chamber -- I believe I sought leave from the Chamber for -- to use with this witness, documents related to the Drina Corps, Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and the 1st Krajina Corps. And it was my understanding that I had received permission from the Chamber to use these documents for the particular purpose that we had described. I thought we had gone -- we had discussed each set of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If that is Mr. Saxon' position and if that's his representation to Court for each of those documents, I don't understand why he is being particularly coy here, using the language for the particular purpose, it's relatively simple what he's doing here. If that's Mr. Saxon's representation and that's what the Office of the Prosecutor is to be bound by with regard to these documents, then obviously they have met their threshold, and I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so the record is very clear, you're using them for the purpose of impeaching.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we look at 65 ter 137, and it should be under tab 20, General Simic, this document is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Saxon. Is this 65 ter 137, or is it XN-137.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is XN-137, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You withdraw -- you have withdrawn XN-133.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. What we see now is XN-137.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, at the upper left-hand corner, we see a stamp from the Command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, do we not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we look in the middle of the -- of the page at the top, it says: "List of documents of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, submitted to the Main Staff of the VRS." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on the upper right-hand corner, which see the word "Drina." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see much more. National defence, state secret, R, Drina, copy number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the page, we see the seal, or the stamp, of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could turn to what is tab 21 in your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you turn, is there any reason why this document is not signed and not dated? It's just for 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to help us with Judge Moloto's question.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not able to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, please, to tab 21, General. And this is -- we are now in the realm of 65 ter XN-138.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm getting a little lost, Mr. Saxon. I thought these XNs were batches of documents that you were dealing with and -- and then when are you done with a particular batch, you then ask for its admission, like you've just done with XN-132.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Point taken, Your Honour. That was also my understanding on Friday afternoon when we discussed this. I have just seen that these documents now relating to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, there are six of them, actually each of them have a separate XN number. That is the only change, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could -- if I could ask to tender, marked for identification, the last document that we saw, which was XN-137, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is why I asked the question. Because I was wondering now what we do with that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: XN-137 is admitted into evidence, marked for identification. May it please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2895, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. Does the Chamber wish to take the first break at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If it is convenient for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We can do it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, if you have the document in tab 21 in front of you, and we're looking now at what is 65 ter XN-138, General, up in the upper left-hand corner of this document it says: "Command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps." Does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it refers to the command post in Pale, dated the 26th of January, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In the right-hand corner, we see People's Defence, state secret, R, Drina, copy number 1; is that correct? Or is that attachment number 1?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay, that's copy number 1. And, General, this is an order for the use of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I apologise, I had to look at the last page to check the signature and the stamp. That's why it took a little bit of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's fine. And again, if you're focussed on the last page, there we see the signature of Commander General Stanislav Galic and the seal of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this order would be -- this order from General Galic would be addressed to all the units of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It doesn't state to whom it was delivered. I assume, on the basis of practice, that that's how it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And the purpose of such an order at the level of a corps would be what?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A directive at the strategic level, in this case for the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, is a command by the corps commander to subordinate units for the execution of their assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And can you please -- actually, I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would seek to tender this document, XN-138, Your Honour, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: XN-138 is admitted and marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2896, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: MR. Simic, can you turn to the next tab, please, that would be tab 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could bring up on e-court what is XN-139, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It has just been brought to my attention that this specific exhibit, P2896 does have translation. Is there any reason why it should be marked for identification? Any other reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we have an English translation, Your Honour, then, no. It -- I don't see the need to have it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then it will be admitted fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, the next document says at the top: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment number 3, copy number 1." And the title of the document is, "Use of anti-aircraft forces and air force." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we look at number 1 below the title, the subtitle refers to the first phase of operations, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what does the paragraph numbered with -- with little number (a) tell us?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it states in the title, sir, use of forces against -- use of forces of the anti-aircraft and aircraft defence. Then it talks also about the army, anti-aircraft, and anti-aircraft [as interpreted] who organise a system of unique unified system of anti-aircraft defence in the territory of the SRK. Also, to form air support, in order to provide air force support. I don't have to continue to read what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, thank you. And if you could just turn your eyes towards the bottom of the page, we see the number 2. Then do we have additional instructions for the second phase of the operation? Is that what that says there, that subtitle 2?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it states. But we just need to throw out the word "subsequent." What is provided for is the use of those forces in the first phase of the operation and in the second phase of the operation; not their use subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And at the bottom of this page and the following page, we see the seal of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2897, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you please turn to tab 23 in your binder, and I believe this is 65 ter XN-139 -- excuse me, 140.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that marking, XN, what you just -- that you referred to. But I am managing to find my way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Consider yourself lucky, General, that you don't need to be thinking about that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is it, XN-140?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see at the top of this document the seal of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps on the upper right-hand corner: Drina, attachment number 6, copy number, I believe it's a 1. I might be mistaken. And, General on the upper left-hand corner, does it not: "Approved by the commander, Major-General Stanislav Galic." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the title of this document, on that page at the top, I believe is: "Plan for moral, psychological activities and information for the Sarajevo Romanija Corps." Am I reading that correctly, or have I made a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could turn -- if we could go forward two pages in e-court. And if you could go forward two pages, General, we see that this document has been signed by the assistant commander Colonel Kosovac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And if you move forward three more pages, through a series of tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could go in e-court to the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I have your indulgence to check one thing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, at this time, I'd like to tender what is XN-140, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number, and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit P2898, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we see what is XN-141, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please stay on the same document, General Simic. You should see some tables. And you'll see, General, that these tables were related to the plan that we just saw. And if we could go to the last page of this document, please. And you should see, General, again the signature of Colonel Ljuban Kosovac. Do you see that, with the seal of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to tell from the different abbreviations here what Colonel Kosovac's position was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll try not to interpret but rather to just to read back. Assistant commander for moral guidance and psychological and political work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender XN-141, please, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned exhibit P2899, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General Simic, if you move to tab 24, please, and if we could pull up on e-court what is XN-142. General Simic, on the far right-hand side we see: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment number 5, copy number 1." And I believe this document is entitled: "Plan for security measures of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on the upper left-hand side, this document has been approved by Major-General Galic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see there the seal of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, could you please move forward three more pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could go do what should be the last page in e-court. We see a series of tables, different items.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, here we see the signature of Colonel Marko Lugonja, with the seal of the SRK Command. Are you with me? I'm sorry, are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document be given a number, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned exhibit P2900, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, if you could turn to tab 25, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could pull up XN-143 on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, does the title of this document say: "Intelligence plan"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see in the upper right-hand corner: "Drina, state secret" -- excuse me, we don't see the word "Drina." We see: "People's Defence, state secret, attachment 4, copy number 1." It says: "Approved by General Galic" on the upper left-hand side. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you turn to the last page, please. And, again, we see the signature of Colonel Lugonja, is that right, and the seal of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Very -- excuse me. General, if you turn to the next -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this be given an exhibit number, XN-143, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given a number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2901, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, if you could turn to the document in tab 26 of your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could call up on the screen what is Exhibit P1556. And we have an English translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm just waiting for the B/C/S now. I'm sorry, I'm waiting for the English to come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, you'll see this document is entitled: "Order for logistics." In the upper right-hand corner it says: "National defence, state secret, R, Drina, attachment number 7, copy number 1." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The upper left-hand corner we see "Sarajevo Romanija Command" in the first line. And then below that, "Pale, PKM." Does PKM stand for rear command post or alternate command post?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute. What is -- is it alternate or rear?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The abbreviation, or acronym, PKM, General, can you tell us, please, in your words, what does it stand for?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each command of an operative or strategic level normally breaks down into two different command posts: Basic command post, rear command post, and reserve command post. This is the rear command post in this case, that of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And we see in the first two lines: "Information on the enemy, number 1. And then number 2 it says: "Organisation of the logistical support." And I'd like you, General, if you could, to help us with something that is on the seventh page in the English version, and the -- I shall find it for you in your version. If you move forward, General, to the fourth page in your version, please, page 4. If we could move forward three more pages in B/C/S, please. And if we could focus on section number 8, which begins about halfway down the page. And will you see, General, that there is a section entitled: "8. Transport support." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And I'm wondering whether you can help us, please, with something in the second paragraph of this section, which says the following in English: "The 27th Logistics Base is in charge of the plans for movement and transportation of material supplies, organisation with the VJ, both en route Rogoj - Trnovo, Pale, Sokolac, and further on towards the destinations in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." Can you explain, General, this phrase about organisation and the VJ, what -- what is the significance of this phrase?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't explain the intention of whoever wrote this, simply because I wasn't involved in this specifically. My answer can be of no relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. We will now -- if we just move to -- we will move from this document. It's been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, those are the documents from the Sarajevo Romanija Corps that we wished to show the witness. The last series of documents are from the 1st Krajina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska. And ... if will you give me one moment to be sure I'm giving you the proper 65 ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: These documents that are coming, are also for the same purpose for impeachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and we left these for today to give the Defence time to review them over the weekend. All right. We have already looked at -- I think I will start -- If we could please provide to General Simic the binder labelled: Volume 1 Drina, please. And ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you turn to tab 11 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we'll be starting, Your Honour, with 65 ter number XN-144. And if we could bring that up on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, in the upper left-hand corner of this document it says: "Command of the 1st Krajina Corps." Does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies, I haven't found the document yet. Yes, that's right. The 1st Krajina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's dated the 21st of January, 1994. We see in the upper right-hand corner: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina." And it says: "Copy number 1." There's a seal in the upper right-hand corner. Is that the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you read to us the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the document is entitled: "Order for defensive/offensive operation."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this document would be an order sent from the command of the Krajina Corps down to subordinate Krajina Corps units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, sir, we skipped the list. This is a single copy. The command of the 1st Krajina Corps, and I'm talking about their documents, in terms of being forwarded to their superiors. This is now being forwarded to the Main Staff of the VRS, which is stated in the previous part of this joint document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, then, just to make things clear, let's leave XN-144 for a moment, and if you could move back one document in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could see what is P1562, please. I'm going to come back to this document in a moment; I just want the record to be clear. I'm just waiting for it to come up on the computer screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There we see again this, General, from the command of the 1st Krajina Corps. This is it P1562. And as you -- as you pointed out, this is a list of 1st Krajina Corps documents submitted to the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see here a list of 14 separate documents. And the document that we looked at just a moment ago, that was the order for defence attack operations, correct, number 1 on the list?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I'm looking at number 1, and the order is not -- the word here is "naredjenje;" the word is "zapovest." Both translate into English as "order." But there is an important difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Can you please explain the difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Zapovest" is more complex document which regulates a very complex use for units in a certain area over a longer period of time. The word "naredjenje," which might also be translated as command, is also command document, but it is normally briefer encompassing no more than two or three details of something to be done on that particular day or over the following days, that being the essential difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right, so a "zapovest," would also then require more time an effort to prepare, is that right, that a "naredjenje," usually?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unless a command is attached to the order. For example, there is a command for logistics, for the rear, or something like that, normally tends to be a little more complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, now can we leave this document, please. And could you turn to the next tab in your binder, and could we look again on e-court at XN-144. So here, General, we see a "zapovest," the more complex form of order for offensive/defensive operations. That's the stamp of the 1st Krajina Corps in the upper right-hand corner, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we please turn to the last page in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could go to your last page, General. And, General, if you could please focus on the last page in subsections 8 and subsection 9. Subsection 9 is a list of attachments, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I've lost track. This is the last page. I have page number five as the last page. And there is no subsection 8. What I see is 4, 5, 6, and 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'm going give you my copy, because I suspect that my copy is more complete than your copy.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I wasn't the one who produced this document, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I know. It is completely -- it is completely our fault. Please, it is no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, are you looking at tab 11 of your binder or tab 12?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirteen, command for the intelligence security. Is that the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No. I apologise. Could you turn back to tab 11 in your binder, please. Do you have a longer document now, in tab 11? Should be about --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have the order that we started discussing a minute ago, order for defence and attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And can you turn to the last page, please. And on that last page, you should see, among other things, a section 8 and a section 9.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what section 8 is telling us.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wording itself speaks for itself. Name - code, the plan for the use of the 1st Krajina Corps. "The plan for the use of the 1st Krajina Corps is to be executed under code-name Drina."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And section 9 is a list of an attachments to this -- to this particular plan or to the order that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. So the subsection 9 refers to a list of attachments to the plan itself.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. All these attachments go up to -- go to make up a plan that is eventually used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And on that last page at the very bottom we see the signature of the Momir Talic, the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps, and it's sealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender XN-144, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted, marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned exhibit P2902, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you please turn to tab 12, General Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could please see XN-145 on the screen. General Simic, if we focus now on the first page of this document, there is a seal of the 1st Krajina Corps on the upper right-hand side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see the words: "Drina, attachment 2, copy number 1." And then I believe the title says: "Order to protect intelligence." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can please turn to the last page of this document. And we see there the signature of General Talic again with the seal of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. So such an order would normally be sent by the corps commander to his assistant for intelligence. Is that how this would be used?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This command is part of the plan for the overall use. The previous order has some attachments which you were asking me about a while ago, what we enumerated a minute ago. This is a command for intelligence security, one of the documents that were part of the plan on how to use that corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this be given an exhibit number, please, and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit P2903, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you turn to tab 13, please, and I believe we are up to XN-146. General, this document -- well, I'll ask you, please. Can you please tell us what this -- what this document is entitled, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the title is: "The plan for intelligence security."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And below those capital letters at the top, there are some smaller letters. Can you tell us what that says, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't understand. I didn't read the entire heading. The entire heading states: "Plan of intelligence security for the execution of the defence and attack operation of the 1st Krajina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on the upper right-hand side we see: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment 3, copy number 1." On the left-hand side, General, we see it says: "Approved by General Talic." Does it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps. Can you please move to the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could see the last page in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see a signature at the bottom. We see the stamp at the upper right-hand corner. And this document was signed by Colonel Djuric. And he was the assistant to the chief of intelligence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be given an exhibit number, please, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Given an exhibit number, please, and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit P2904, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn, please, to 65 ter -- excuse me. Can you turn to tab 14, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we please see XN-147, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this document is entitled: "Plan for camouflage;" is that correct? Or do I need to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for my sake. But for the transcript, yes, it states, "Plan of operations tactical camouflage."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. On the upper right-hand side we see: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment number 4, copy number 1." On the left-hand side, it says: "Approved by the Commander, Momir Talic." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we just look in column 2, at the very top, the title of that column. It says: "Taskings for operative camouflage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you move, please, to the last page of the document. And on the bottom right-hand corner we see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps. And then below that, the signature of Colonel Stanimir Stanimirovic. And colonel Stanimirovic was the chief of operations and training for the 1st Krajina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So when this plan was produced it was Colonel Stanimirovic who signed off on it and sent it up to General Talic; is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see that this document is signed at the end by Colonel Stanimirovic, so he would have been the officer in the 1st Krajina Corps who signed off on this plan at the end when it was produced, in order to provide it to General Talic for his approval.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to give a broader explanation, if you permit, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Stanimirovic was the chief for operations and training of the corps, and he participated in the development of the overall plan for use of forces. This is something that is done at the command post in the operations room; it's a team effort. And when he drafted it, he submitted it to his commander for approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And who was his commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the commander was Momir Talic. That is what it states in the document. But we are looking at a document -- we're looking at individual documents that comprise the overall plan of use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Simic. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please be given an exhibit number, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is given an exhibit number. May it please be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this document shall be assigned exhibit P2905, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
