utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you please move to tab 15 in your binder. And could we please see on e-court XN-148, please. General, it says "plan" at the very top of the page. Can you read to us, please, the rest of the title that is underneath the word "plan."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it states: "Plan of security measures of the 1st Krajina Corps for the defence and attack operation."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. In the upper right-hand corner we see: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment number 5, copy number 1." General, in the upper left-hand side again we see -- this has been approved by the commander of the corps, Momir Talic; has it not. If you look at the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the last page, please. We see the seal of the Sarajevo -- excuse me. We see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps at the top. And below, we see a signature, and this plan was signed by the chief of the security department, Colonel Bogojevic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please be given an exhibit number, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2906, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you please turn to tab 16 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could we please call on e-court, XN-149.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this is a plan for anti-electronic combat; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does that mean jamming, or does that mean -- does that mean jamming the communications of the enemy, or counter-jamming the communications of the enemy? Can you explain.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer until I look at the entire document. There's electronic surveillance. Then there is EO, electronic jamming, anti-electronic combat, and anti-surveillance protection. So what you have asked me is actually part of electronic surveillance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. What does anti-electronic combat mean? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word itself, anti-electronic combat, means that we would be monitoring the communications of the enemy, finding out their intentions and protecting our own communications from enemy surveillance. That is it, simply put. And if you permit me to say, for the sake of clarification, the column of assignments, it says, Electronic surveillance, uncover and monitor radio communications of special and other forces which preparing, and so on and so forth. I don't want to take up any more time by reading the entire thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, that's fine. Thank you. But when you refer to the particular column of assignments, can you just tell us which column you're looking at. Where is it? Is it the first column on the left? Or is it the column that says "zadaci," and then it has a number 2 below it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Zadaci," assignments. That is that column that I'm thinking of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for correcting me. Can you please turn to the last page of this document, General Simic. We see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps, and the signature, again, Stanimirovic, Stanimir. And then we see two words which are difficult for me. "Nacelnik," and then it is either a word or an abbreviation. Can you tell what that stands for?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the chief of the organ for operations and training. That is where we -- earlier we saw the chief of the section, and now we have the chief of the organ of operations and training, which means that this is at a higher level than the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may this be given an exhibit number marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2907, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, can you please turn to what is tab 17 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we please pull up in e-court XN-150.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this document is entitled - I hope I'm correct, and you'll correct me if I'm not - "Order for electronic surveillance and jamming." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see in the upper right-hand corner: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment 7," it looks like "copy 1," and then the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps. Can you just take a moment to look at this document, and can you explain to us how does this document relate to the previous document that we just looked at, which had to do with anti-electronic combat, or what's the difference between the two, if you can explain?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This plan of anti-electronic combat is a plan approved by the commander. It was developed by the person who developed it, and the commander approved it. Out of that would result a command for those who were meant to execute this plan, or, better said, a command --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. So this document here is -- is the command that was produced, is that right? According to the plan.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you're asking me as if I was the one who developed this programme. I'm just talking on the basis of my experience. An operative officer developed a plan and the plan was approved by the commander. On the basis of that plan, tasks would be pulled out and drafted in the form of a command for those who were meant to implement certain actions as part of the overall plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you turn to the last page, please. We see on the last page this document has been signed by Commander Momir Talic. We see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document be given an exhibit number, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2908, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you please turn to the document that is in tab 18 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we please see on e-court XN-151, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The heading on the document states: "Plan of electronic surveillance and jamming."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. It's been approved, on the upper left-hand corner by General Talic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Upper right-hand side we see Drina, attachment 8, copy 1. Could you please turn to the last page, General. We see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps in the upper right hand. And towards the bottom we see the signature of Colonel Djuric, and is he signing this document on behalf of the intelligence branch? Is that what we see there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states in the document that he signed it as assistant chief of intelligence, because surveillance is part of the intelligence activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be given an exhibit number, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit P2909, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you please turn to tab 19 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could please see on e-court XN-152, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this is an order for engineering support; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see on the upper right-hand corner: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment number 9, copy number 1." And we see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps. And could you please take a look at the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we scroll down, please, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see here that this order is signed by General Talic and it's been sealed -- it has the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please be given an exhibit number, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit P2910, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, could you please turn to tab 20, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can call up on e-court, XN-153.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, if you could focus on the first page for now of this document. The title is: Plan for morale and psychological activities an information. But can you tell me what the last part of the title says because I'm not able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it states: "In units of the 1st Krajina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We see this plan on the upper left-hand corner has been approved by Momir Talic. We see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps. In the upper right-hand corner, we see the words: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment number 10, copy number 1." Could you turn to the last page of this document, General. At the bottom right-hand corner of this table, we see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps, and then we see a signature of Colonel -- I believe it is Vukelic. And we see a series of abbreviations above his name. Are you able to tell us what his position was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you an answer. I can just read what it states. I don't know all of those people. I didn't know all the people who were in the Army of Yugoslavia, to be able to tell who was who at lower ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sure. But my question is a little -- and I understand that limitation. But my question was a little bit different. Just from the acronyms that we see above the word "Colonel," are you able to tell us what the gentleman's position was? For example, is there a reference to moral and religious affairs, for example?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm reading, assistant commander for moral guidance, religious issues and political and propaganda affairs. I am not familiar with their precise establishment structure to be able to tell you more. That was not one of my assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Fine, thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this document could be given an exhibit number, please, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit P2911, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you please turn, General, to tab 21 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we please see XN-154, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, this is an order for anti-aircraft defence, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see, after -- the acronym PVO, we see some other acronyms in smaller letters. Can you tell us what that means, Op.Br.1?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The heading literally states: "Order for anti-aircraft defence, operational number 1."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And that is the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps next to the title?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see the word: "Drina, attachment 11, copy number 1." Could you turn to the last page of this document, please, General. And this document has been signed by Colonel Milosevic, Petar Milosevic, and according to his title here with the -- above -- above the word "Colonel," he was the chief for anti-aircraft and artillery. Is that right? For the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Please -- please clarify.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that that is the chief of the artillery and rocket units of the anti-aircraft defence of the Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this please be given an exhibit number, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so given an exhibit number. May it please be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P2912, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you please turn to tab 22 of your binder, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we please see XN-155, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this is a list of documents related to the plan of communications for the 1st Krajina Corps; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a list of documents of the plan of communications of the command of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. We see at the top right-hand corner, People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment number 12, copy number 1. At the bottom of the page --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move forward two pages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this is an order for communications. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see the word "Drina" up top, "attachment 12, copy 1." Number 1, it says: "Communications centres." Towards the top of the first page. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Communication centres, yes, you are quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if you could move forward two more pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see this particular order came from Major-General Kelecevic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that's the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're correct. But it states the Chief of Staff of that corps. It states: "Chief of Staff, Major-General," and then below that "Kelecevic." So he has a communications organ in his staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And if you turn the page, General - if we go forward one more page in e-court - we see here a chart for radio communications of the 1st Krajina Corps. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A chart for radio communications of the 1st Krajina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. And in the upper right-hand corner we see: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment 1, copy 1." Below that we see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you move forward one page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How many more pages are you going to be moving forward, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Six, Your Honour. If you prefer, we can break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If that is convenient for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will take a break and come back at a quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We're still looking at XN-155. And, General Simic, if you could focus on the document in front of you. This document is an overview of times when frequencies must be changed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see in the upper right-hand corner, it says: "People's Defence, state secret, Drina, attachment 1a, copy number 1." At the bottom we see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps Command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The next page, Mr. Simic, we see at the top centre, the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps Command. And this is a chart of radio communications, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So this would show radio communications of -- between different units of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 1st Krajina Corps Command and its subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On this page, we see - and if we could focus in on the top line for a moment - this is a chart of coded communications for the Command of the 1st Krajina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, first of all, we see in the middle of the page a series of lines connecting circles and rectangles. And then below that we see additional rectangles with different items going down vertically. This represents the fact that within coded communications there are different machines and different networks that are used.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps Command at the bottom. We see Drina at the top, attachment number 5, copy number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This page is an overview of secret call-signs for the Command of the 1st Krajina Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not entirely right. We see what it says, overview of code-names for the 1st Krajina Corps Command. But these are also code-names of their subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And if we look over to the left-hand side, just beneath the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps Command, in the second column we see a list of commands, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see all of the participants in the chain of command of the Krajina Corps and its superior, starting with the President of Republika Srpska; number 2, the Government of Republika Srpska, and so on and so forth. The Main Staff of the VRS command post, the Main Staff of the VRS rear command post. So this relates to all of the participants from the Krajina Corps Command down to their subordinates and also those above them, their superiors, when communicating with them, they use encryption.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. If you move your focus toward the right side of the page, we also see there, first of all, call-signs for the Republika Srpska Krajina, is that right, and their corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which -- which side of the -- which column on the right side of the page, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm referring to the second full column from the right edge of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you see there across two columns at the top it says: "Republika Srpska Krajina." So in that section, General, we see the Government of the Republika Srpska Krajina and -- then followed by the Main Staff of the Army of Srpska Krajina followed by the different corps of the Army of Srpska Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that we see the words running across the two columns "Army of Yugoslavia" or "Yugoslav Army."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And below that we can see the command of the VJ General Staff, below that, the command -- the rear command of the VJ General Staff, and a number of units below that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Okay. Please explain.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said the command, but that's not what it says. It says the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, command post. And then the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, rear command post, and so on. That would be the exact translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much for clarifying that. Thank you. And if we go to the next page, please. The next page contains the telephone information or -- of particular officers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And we see in the upper left-hand side the seal of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender what is XN-155, marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned exhibit P2913, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General Simic, since Friday, we've looked at a lot of documents related to the so-called Drina Plan, which is more formally titled the directive for use of the Yugoslav Army, the Republika Srpska army, and the Serb army of Krajina. And you and I have looked at documents produced by the VRS Main Staff that were sent to the corps level of the VRS. And we've looked at a number of documents produced by the 1st Krajina Corps and by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. The -- the preparations of these documents that we've looked at, it would require thousands of man hours, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hardly say. There were different levels at which this was done. I don't know how many levels exactly. I can't be very specific about that, but it probably took some time, with many people involved, at different levels of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "it probably took some time," it probably took, at a minimum, a number of weeks of time; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the level of command. It's very difficult for me say specifically. I was not involved in producing these documents myself. Therefore, I can hardly be expected to provide an adequate answer. It depends on the level of training and all sorts of things. Someone might take two-hours to draft a document, another person might take three hours for that same document. That is what makes it impossible for me to answer your question with a greater degree of specificity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, just before I forget, looks like you're going to move to a new topic. What do you plan to do with XN-133?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I am --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It has not been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just check that this explanation accords with your position. I have been told that it was withdrawn because it was a whole set of Drina Corps documents and because they were now admitted separately, that is why it was withdrawn. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In a nutshell that is correct, Your Honour, it has been withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct. So I can write "withdrawn" against it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to discuss with you, General Simic, part of the discussion that you had with Mr. Lukic last week. On page 10056 of the transcript, starting at line 25, to 10058, line 2, you explained your position that the VJ, the VRS, and the SVK were always separate and equal armies. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, these were three different armies. There is no subordination there, no superiors and no subordinates, if that's what's been recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness P1896. And so if he could be given the binder that says P and D, please, and find the tab P1896.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Take a moment to look at that document, please, General Simic. These are the minutes from the official talk about transfer to the VRS that were recorded on the 11th of September, 1994, in the office of the Drina Corps Command, recruitment and personnel affairs section chief on the occasion of transfer of Lieutenant-Colonel Erak, to the 30th Personnel Centre. And if you will follow me, General, you will see in the first full paragraph, it says that: "During the official talk, the above mentioned Erak was shown a written notice that his wife Zlata requested from a VJ senior in charge to return him to the service in the Zrenjanin garrison from which he was dispatched to the Republika Srpska Army ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it continues: "And so he also needed to express his opinion about his transfer ..." And then with subletter (a) below that, subparagraph (a), we see that Lieutenant-Colonel Erak said the following: "No one asked me for opinion regarding my transfer to 30th Personnel Centre. I have been transferred seven times so far, and I am of the opinion that in accordance with Article 34 of the above-mentioned decree, I should not have been transferred to VRS without my personal consent; I have refused to be transferred ..." Do you see that, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm following you every step of the way, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then subparagraph (b) says: "I have been transferred to the Army of Republika Srpska in accordance with Article 58 of the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia. And on the same ground, I should not have and could not have been transferred to the 30th Personnel Centre."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could please go to the next page in English, please, and the next page -- if you could turn the page in your version. And next page in English -- in the B/C/S version in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, General, if you focus on subparagraph (f), it says: "Based on the above-mentioned, I request to be returned to the Zrenjanin garrison from which I had been transferred to the Army of Republika Srpska as soon as possible ..." And then below that we see section 3: "Conclusion of the senior who conducted the official talk." And, General, just to help us, the term "senior" here refers to the senior officer who conducted the official talk; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And if we take a look at the conclusion of that senior officer, it says -- first of all, it says: "The corps command does not possess the personnel [sic] record of the above-mentioned Erak, and so they could not confirm all of his assertions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not personnel record, personal record. That's what is written on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour, I stand corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After that, it says: "The corps command senior personnel is manned with 23 per cent of its capacity, so every senior is precious for performing duties." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm following you every step of the way, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And a few lines below that, it says: "He has been in the Army of Republika Srpska since 13 December 1993 until now." And then it says: "Most of the seniors," that is, senior officers, "have various problems. And if everyone's requests were granted, we would have no more seniors. Should the request of the above-mentioned Erak be granted, we request that another senior be deployed here." General Simic, doesn't -- don't these conclusions of the senior officer suggest that the VRS had a certain dependence on the VJ for senior officers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that would be my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does -- doesn't this suggest a strong connection between the senior officer corps of the VJ and the senior officer corps of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What sort of connection do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That members of the officer corps of the VJ are -- are filling the senior officer positions of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about an area in which I'm no specialist. I don't want my answer to lead the Chamber to conclude something that is erroneous. There are persons that are witness who actually dealt with this sort of issue. I believe they will be better placed than I am to provide a valid answer to that query.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, General Simic, you testified that these were separate armies. So, you see, it was you, actually, who provided your opinion, and that's what -- that's what I'm trying to explore with you. And my question is, how separate, really, were they if they were sharing the officer corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said at one point that there were three different armies. Now that was not just my opinion. It is an explicit assertion on my part. There are three different armies and three different chains of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness, please, P399.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't seem to track that down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can the usher please assist the witness to find the tab that says P399.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could take a moment, General, to familiarise yourself with this document. It's from the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It has a number, confidential number 21/32-21, dated the 3rd of February, 1994, and it's signed by Commander Lieutenant-general Ratko Mladic. And in the preamble it says the following -- in your version, General, you will see General Mladic's signature on the bottom of the second page. And in the preamble it says: "Pursuant to Article 26 of the Rules on travel and other expenses in the VJ and in connection with the implementation of the decision identifying tasks and territory of service under difficult (special) conditions, the General Staff VJ, the sector for operations, confidential number 1296-I of 19 October 1993, I hereby adopted the following decision on compensation for military service in difficult (special) conditions." Let's just stick with the preamble for a moment, please, General. What General Mladic is saying in the preamble is that he adopted a decision as the commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, based on the Rules of the Army of Yugoslavia and a decision of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia? Doesn't that suggest that the VJ and the VRS were not so separate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I find the question a little ambiguous.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, we have a preamble from the commander of the VRS Main Staff based on rules of the Army of Yugoslavia and a decision of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. Doesn't that suggest that these two armies had some pretty strong connections? You said they were separate armies.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it, and I'm still saying it. They were separate armies, in terms of chain of command. As for what you are asking about, my administration drafted a command by the chief of the General Staff, saying that those officers working under difficult circumstances would be paid a supplement. Given the fact that this went through the personnel centres and officers went to join the VRS of their own free will, there was a need to deal with their rights, given their status, and this was how it was done. This certainly in no way implies a chain of command. Let me try to be even more specific. If a chain of command was implied here, then the documents from the Army of Yugoslavia would be worded as commands to be dispatched to both Main Staffs, yet that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, just so that I understand your position, sir, in your previous testimony, you said, "The VJ, the VRS, and the SVK were always separate and equal," at page 10056 of the transcript to 10058. And your position is now that they were separate armies in terms of chains of command; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me the same question in two different ways. I am not sure about how the word "equal" was interpreted the way I got it. If you could explain what you mean by "equal," perhaps I can go on and answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I can't explain what you meant. I can only read what is in the transcript. It was your testimony that -- that was translated as "separate and equal."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I was misunderstood the first time around, let me try and explain it now. These are three different armies. Each of these armies has its own chain of command. They are on an equal footing and on an equal level. There is no subordination in the sense of there being no superiors or indeed subordinates. I'm not sure if I'm making myself any clearer now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think understand your testimony. I want to focus on what you just said, these are three different armies. There were strong connections between the VJ, the VRS, and the SVK; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the Prosecutor should explain what exactly he means by "strong connections."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to allow the witness to answer without being confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The first point I would like to raise is, haven't you asked this question already?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I have, I shall move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you did, actually. Let's see if we can get where you said it. I don't want to gag you. Okay, I'm not finding it quickly enough, so you might as well answer the question. And then Mr. Lukic wants to understand what you mean by "strong connection."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At many different levels, General Simic, for example, the VJ and the VRS had very strong relations; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by "strong relations." What exactly do you have in mind? In an army, there can be cooperation, there can be coordination, and there can be subordination. There is no third -- no fourth kind of relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I -- I think I want to explore that with you a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The strong connections were mentioned at page 69, line 17. Question was: "Well, we have a preamble for the commander of the VRS Main Staff based on the rules of the Army of Yugoslavia and a decision of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. Doesn't that suggest that these two armies had some pretty strong connections?"

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to -- if we can show the witness what is P741, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, I am going to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we take a look at this document, General -- do you have it in front of you? P741?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, Mr. Prosecutor, I've got that, and I'm exceptionally familiar this. This was produced by my administration, and you will see my initials there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. And so this was the decision on determining the tasks and territory where service is performed under difficult or (special) conditions; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And this is dated 22nd of March, 1994. And, of course, the second paragraph -- second full paragraph, after "Decision: It includes the territory where members of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres are in service."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we now please show the witness P1810, please. Can we assist the witness to find tab P1810.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document is from Military Post 3001, Belgrade, that was the 30th Personnel Centre. Correct, General?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so. It has been a long time. I can't be certain, but I assume that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. It's dated the 12th of May, 1994. And it's a decision, says in the preamble: "Pursuant to Article 156 of the Law on of Army of Yugoslavia, published in the Official Gazette and in relation to the decision of the Army of Yugoslavia, chief of the General Staff, regarding the determining of tasks and territories where service is carried out under aggravated (exceptional) conditions, hereby issues the following ..." So it refers to the document that we saw a moment ago, which was P741, and then we see the decision: "Mladic, son of Nedjo, Ratko, lieutenant-general, serving with the military post 3001 Belgrade," that is the 30th personnel centre, "is herewith entitled to compensation for service under aggravated (exceptional) conditions as follows ..." And so, subparagraph (a): "In the amount of 20 per cent of his basic salary. And then subparagraph (b), it says: "Increase of compensation mentioned under (a) in the amount of blank per cent of the basic salary ... and the decision of the Commander of Military Post 3001, Belgrade," and that would have been General Mladic himself, "number 21/32-21, dated 3 February 1994." And that last document mentioned there was Exhibit P399, which was the decision of General Mladic from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska that I showed you a moment ago, on compensation for military service in difficult or (special) conditions. So we see this document in front of us. It's a document from the Army of Yugoslavia, from the 30th Personnel Centre. It refers to the decision that you helped draft, regarding the determining of territories where service is carried out under aggravated conditions; that was P741. It refers to General Mladic as serving in Military Post 3001, that is, the 30th Personnel Centre. And then in subparagraph (b), it also relies on the decision of the Commander of Military Post 3001, Belgrade, which was actually General Mladic's decision issued by the VRS Main Staff. That was P399 that I showed you a few minutes ago. So it seems, General, that this document show -- we have a VJ decision about compensation to be paid to Ratko Mladic that's partly based on a VRS decision issued by Ratko Mladic and partly based on a decision of the VJ General Staff. And my question for you is, doesn't this contradict your proposition that these were two separate armies?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Permit me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We adopted a decision for certain compensation for work under difficult circumstances, and the personnel administration of the 30th Personnel Centre had the superior officer go to Republika Srpska, and the chain of command in the Yugoslav Army was severed and that person became a member of the chain of command of Republika Srpska, but their rights stemming from the employment had to be resolved because of their families that had stayed in the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And from that point of view, we cannot mix up the chain of command with the exercise of certain rights and application of certain entitlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, first of all, you told us earlier that -- I was asking about an area in which you're not a specialist but you seemed to be willing to get into that area for a moment at least. If I understand you -- you see, what I don't understand from your response, if we stick with the documents that we've been looking at, because I haven't asked you about a chain of command, I just don't understand how, if you have a single document, and in this sense, in this situation right now, we have a document issued by the Army of Yugoslavia that incorporates in it -- and that document is referring to an officer who is ostensibly serving in a position in the Army of Yugoslavia, but, in reality, he is serving in a position in the Army of Republika Srpska, and that same VJ document relies on a decision issued by that same officer, which he issued in his capacity as an officer of the Army of Republika Srpska, doesn't it suggest that, really, these two armies were very mixed up together, rather than separate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is a really complex question than Mr. Saxon would need to simplify it. It's a question that begins on page 25 [sic], line 10, and goes to line 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will simplify it. I think that's a fair point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Doesn't the document that you have in front of you indicate that, really, the VJ and the VRS were really mixed up together, rather than separate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that does not mean that, and I cannot really explain anymore this document. I said that I was not an expert. I've told you what I know. I'm sure there are persons who are more qualified to explain. I am not really able to give you any more detailed explanations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I'm going to move onto another topic now. During your direct examination, you -- you described and you discussed with Mr. Lukic the work of the operations centre of the VJ General Staff, and you also talked about the daily reports issued by that operation centre, and I just want to make sure that I understand what your position is. We saw a number of reports issued by that operations centre. The daily reports that I believe would have gone up to the chief of the General Staff. But my question for you is: Is it your position that the universe of information available to Momcilo Perisic when he was the chief of the General Staff was limited to the contents of the daily reports from the operations centre?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand whether you meant overall informations or daily combat reports. I would just like you to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try to use your language. Was that the only -- was the information contained in the daily reports from the operations centre the only information available to General Perisic about what was happening in the FRY in the conflict areas?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And, so, for example, can we take look, please, at D200?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think it might be helpful if we could assist -- do you have D200 there? No, it's fine, General, do not worry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if that is the document, D202.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It was 65 ter -- it was 65 ter 1114D. So that would be in another binder. It's now Exhibit D200.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to -- I'm going to try to do this another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The 2nd Administration would send reports to the chief of the General Staff, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that earlier, and if you allow me, when I said that daily combat reports were not the only source of information, he also received reports from the 2nd Administration, the Security Administration, the Ministry of Interior, from State Security, from certain government ministries and other sources, from the superiors there. These were sources of information for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we -- actually, I have hopefully hard copies. I do. If we can please call up D222 on the ELMO, and I have a hard copy for the witness. If this could be given to him, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Have you now abandoned D200?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I have abandoned it, Your Honour. If we could see D222 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you saw this, I believe, it was on Thursday, during your direct examination, General Lukic [sic]. It's discussed at pages 10094 to 10095 of the transcript. And if you could please direct your attention to the first paragraph. It's the intelligence report dated the 13th July, 1995. And you will see it begins with information about how VRS units have routed the 28th Division of the Muslim army from Srebrenica. And if you'd please look at the last sentence of that paragraph, it says the following: "So far, about 50 per cent of Muslim residents" -- the last sentence of that paragraph, General: "About 50 per cent of Muslims residents have been evacuated from the Srebrenica area; the evacuation of the remaining residents is made difficult by a shortage of vehicles." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now can we please show the witness what is Prosecution Exhibit P855. I have a copy for the witness. If you could show that to Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told these are confidential exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could move to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please see Exhibit P2169, please. And that should be in the witness's binder. Actually, could we please go to -- no, I will stay with this document for a moment. If we could -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document is from the 5th of May, 1995. And early May 1995, General, that was the time of Operation Flash in Western Slavonia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And we see that this particular document -- it's from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. And it's submitted to a number of corps, and the Main Staff of the -- a number of corps of the Army of Republika Srpska. And then in the second paragraph, in the second line, we see that it's submitted to the Main Staff of the Yugoslav Army. You see that? Second line of the second paragraph. Or it may --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we could move down the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see that: "The concern is that due to the new situation in the RSK and a suspicion that the documents of the communications plan in Western Slavonia have fallen into the hands of the enemy, the existing code-names of the units and commands shall be changed, according to the following ..." And then we see a list of units, commands and different code-names. This particular document shows an ongoing relationship of communication, doesn't it, between the Army of Yugoslavia, the VRS, and the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not dispute that there were communications there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this relationship was close -- so close that the VJ would have the code-names of all of the units and commands of the VRS and the SVK; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The close relationship was a friendly relationship arising from the interest of the Army of Yugoslavia for the sake of its security to be constantly informed about what was going on in that area. And to take timely measures in the Army of Yugoslavia in order to prevent any possible surprises or any threats to its own security. From that aspect were these documents also in our possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And following up on the point that you just made, can we move into private session, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is Exhibit P2764, please. He might need the help of the usher to find that particular tab. And I'm very grateful to the usher for her support today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I have just been informed it is not in the binder. I will check to see if I have a hard copy, which I do not. I will skip this document. If we could move back into public session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness P1824. This is not the ... this is not the document that I was expecting to see. Is this P1824? I'm asking -- this is P1824. Then I'm going to move again away from this document. I will try again. Can we please see P1933. Okay. And if we could focus on the first half of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at this document, General Simic, you'll see that it is entitled: "Situation and activities of the Serbian army of Krajina, VRS, and VJ." And then under number 1, we see: "General features of the situation and status of the activities." Followed by the line: "General Perisic's visit to the SVK 1st Corps." And in the first sentence of the first paragraph it says that on the 8th and 9th of July, Momcilo Perisic visited the area of responsibility of the 11th East Slavonian corps in an official capacity. After he visited units of Baranjska Division on July 9th in the morning, he convened a meeting of the 11th Corps Command and then left for Aljmas accompanied by General Dusan Loncar, commander of the 11th Corps. There he met with Milan Milanovic, also known as Mrgud, assistant minister of defence of the RSK." And then below that we see: "The purpose and the main topic of these visits and meetings were to boost combat readiness of the Serbian army of Krajina in the occupied territories of Eastern Slavonia and Baranja, as well as to ascertain direction of further cooperation with the SVK and assistance to be provided to the Army of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To be provided --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "... by the army of Yugoslavia." Thank you Your Honour. And again -- if we could stick with the first sentence of that paragraph, General, if you help us understand, please, why was it General Perisic's business to boost of combat readiness of the SVK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to ask, I don't know if the witness was able to look at the whole document to see whose document that was. I don't think that we can see that from the first page. Perhaps before the General answers, he could look at the whole document or perhaps the Prosecutor could tell him who actually generated this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would you like do take a moment and look at the next page, if you haven't had a moment to do that, General Simic? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who send the document. It says here "intelligence information," and then there's a number, class 8040895, then there's the register number 512-06-06. We don't use this kind of marking system so this is why I'm asking where the document comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I can only say that the document speaks for itself. The document says what it says.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not quite like that, sir. If the document came from the intelligence administration of the other side, perhaps deliberately misrepresented the situation, so -- as to the contents of the document, so this is why I'm asking you who generated the document because it does not seem to be in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the last -- the last page of this document in the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Chief Davor Domazet. So this would have been generated by a Croatian officer then. I'm just trying to answer your inquiry.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croatian officer, yes. I could tell by the style, by the language, that that was that. That's the style. So if you understood me, that the intelligence administration could be planting some information, then it's possible that that was so, but I cannot know whether Perisic was there or not. It's something that I cannot confirm. I does not have to be accountable to me. I am the one who is accountable to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
